Name: coverage_not_headcount
Title: Coverage, Not Headcount: What a Population of Writers Adds to an Agent's Experience Store at Matched Collection Cost
Short Hypothesis: At a fixed total collection budget, an experience store written by several policies is worth more to a reader than the reader's own store only by the task-type coverage the other writers add (types on which some writer succeeds more often than the reader), a statistic computable from the writers' collection logs before any reading. Once coverage, budget and per-type item counts are held fixed by construction, the number of writers (2 vs 8), the class of their diversity (scaffold/temperature variants of the reader's backbone vs other backbones) and the retrieval-time conflict among their items each move the reader's gain by less than the Gate-0 effect of 6 net, whereas a coverage change at the same budget and headcount moves it by at least that much; displacing half of the reader's own budget by a writer it dominates on every type costs nothing.
Related Work: Memory Sharing (2404.09982) and Multi-Agent Transactive Memory (2606.19911) show that pooling contributions from several agents helps a reader, but pool at unmatched cost, do not vary the number or kind of contributing policies, and never compare against a pool the reader collected itself with the same episodes. 'Scaling Teams or Scaling Time' (2604.03295) reports non-monotonic scaling with team size when experience is reused, as a conceptual view with one backbone and no matched-budget stores; 'Understanding Agent Scaling via Diversity' (2602.03794) bounds inference-time ensembles by the number of complementary channels, not stored experience. StateFuse (2607.05844) preserves conflicts among replicas but does not measure how store value changes with writer count or diversity. In the imitation-learning home literature, demonstration compatibility across multiple human demonstrators (2210.08073) predicts multi-demonstrator IL success for a trained policy, not for an in-context reader at matched budget. The archived contributor_conflict_not_size claimed cross-contributor conflict degrades shared libraries with conflict a property of its construction; here conflict is manipulated at fixed coverage and headcount and coverage is the pre-read predictor. The archived closer_beats_stronger claimed policy proximity, not capability, predicts transfer; here a far-but-covering writer and a near-but-dominated writer are the two arms that decide between proximity and coverage.
Abstract: Shared experience stores are now written by several agents, but their value is reported at unmatched cost, with one kind of writer, and never against the pool a reader could have collected itself with the same episodes. We ask what a population of writers adds at a fixed collection budget B and propose that the answer is a statistic computable from the writers' collection logs before any reading: the coverage complement C, the validation-weighted excess of the best writer's per-type success over the reader's own. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B, EXAONE-4.0-32B and gpt-oss-120b as writers and readers, and scaffold and temperature variants of Qwen3-32B as proximity manipulations at fixed capability, we manipulate coverage, headcount, diversity class and retrieval conflict separately at the same budget: a two-writer store that adds coverage is compared with a two-writer store of identical item count that adds none; an eight-writer store is built to have exactly the coverage complement and per-type item counts of the two-writer store; four-writer stores of identical coverage differ only in whether their extra writers are proximity or capability variants; and eight-writer stores of identical coverage are filtered to one procedure skeleton per type or spread across skeletons. Every store is read with the same retriever at k=3 and reported per writer x reader cell as the retained-gain ratio against the reader's own matched-cost pool, net of a static procedure prompt, with a planted-harm positive control establishing that the pipeline detects a Gate-0 loss. We predict that a coverage change at fixed headcount moves gain by at least 6 net, that headcount, diversity class and conflict at fixed coverage each move it by less than 6 (two one-sided tests at 8 seeds), that displacing half the reader's budget by a writer it dominates on every type costs nothing, that model writers recover at least 60% of the expert writer's contribution at matched item count, and, secondarily, that C rank-correlates with gain across 21 store x reader cells.
Experiments:
- Writers and pools. B = 3,553 train episodes (the on-disk Qwen3-32B ReAct self pool, 1,892 successes). Each additional writer collects B/2 episodes on a random half of the train games (disjoint halves for pairs; the eighths used for N=8 are nested inside the halves), success-filtered, same trajectory format: Qwen3-32B plan-then-act; Qwen3-32B ReAct at T=0.7; Qwen3-32B ReAct with a self-check turn; Qwen3-32B ReAct at T=1.2 (the pre-registered dominated writer); EXAONE-4.0-32B ReAct and gpt-oss-120b ReAct at the full B (they are also those readers' self pools; halves reused); gpt-oss-120b plan-then-act at B/2 (eighth writer). Expert walkthroughs (1,465 items, no episode cost) are an item-matched writer reported separately. Per-writer per-type success profiles s_w(t) are logged at collection. Collection: 4 x 1,777 + 3,553 + 3,553 + 1,777 = 15,991 episodes.
- Predictor. Coverage complement C(S,R) = sum_t w_t * max(0, max_{w in S with items retained on t} s_w(t) - s_R(t)), w_t the validation type share; computed from collection logs and frozen, together with every store's composition, before the first evaluation cell.
- Stores at matched budget B (Qwen3-32B reader unless noted). SELF = self(B). DOM = self(B/2)+dominated(B/2): T=1.2 if s_w(t) <= s_self(t) on all six types; if it exceeds self on a type, its items on that type are dropped and the store is per-type item-count-equalized to SELF, so C(DOM) = 0 by construction. COV = self(B/2)+gpt-oss(B/2). Pairs self(B/2)+X(B/2) for X in {EXAONE, plan-then-act, T=0.7, self-check}. HCM (HET-cap-model, N=3) = {Qwen3 ReAct, EXAONE, gpt-oss} at B/3 each (capability and family varied at fixed ReAct scaffold; no expert). HCM-item = HCM subsampled per type to the expert bank's per-type item counts (item-matched; P4 numerator). HCE (N=4) = HCM writers plus the expert item-matched at a quarter share (the earlier HET-cap; secondary cell). HP4 (HET-prox, N=4) = four Qwen3-32B variants at B/4 (proximity varied at fixed capability). ALL8 = all eight model writers at B/8. EC8 (equal-coverage N=8) = the same eight writers at B/8, with the six writers other than self and gpt-oss retaining items only on types t where s_w(t) <= max(s_self(t), s_gptoss(t)), then per-type item-count-equalized to COV (symmetric: COV is subsampled if EC8 is short on a type), so C(EC8) = C(COV) and per-type counts are identical while N rises from 2 to 8. EC4-prox = self(B/4)+gpt-oss(B/4)+{plan-then-act, T=0.7}(B/4 each, restricted as in EC8); EC4-cap = self(B/4)+gpt-oss(B/4)+{EXAONE ReAct, gpt-oss plan-then-act}(B/4 each, restricted): identical C, N and per-type counts, differing only in the class of the extra writers. EC8-skel1 / EC8-skelV = EC8's item pool filtered per type to the modal procedure skeleton (programmatic ALFWorld action parser) versus sampled to spread evenly over the skeletons present, at identical per-type counts and with at least one item per retained writer-type pair; C is recomputed on retained pairs and must match within 0.01, else that type is relaxed to its two most common skeletons. HARM = COV with 25% of the gpt-oss items replaced by manufactured wrong-procedure items (another type's skeleton applied to the item's objects), rerun at 50% if 25% does not reach Gate 0.
- Reading. Same retriever and injection as Measurement A, k=3 for every cell; readers Qwen3-32B (all stores above), EXAONE-4.0-32B (self_EX(B), self_EX(B/2)+Qwen3(B/2), self_EX(B/2)+gpt-oss(B/2), HCM, ALL8) and gpt-oss-120b (self_go(B), self_go(B/2)+Qwen3(B/2), HCM). 274 validation games (seen+unseen).
- Cells and episodes (274 games; 2/4/8 seeds = 548/1,096/2,192 episodes). Qwen3-32B reader: 8 seeds SELF, DOM, COV, EC8 (8,768); 4 seeds static-procedure, self(B/2) alone, HCM, HCM-item, expert-only, EC4-prox, EC4-cap, EC8-skel1, EC8-skelV, HARM (10,960); 2 seeds k=0, the four pairs, HCE, HP4, ALL8 (4,384): 24,112. EXAONE reader: 4 seeds self_EX(B), HCM; 2 seeds k=0, static, two pairs, ALL8: 4,932. gpt-oss reader: 4 seeds self_go(B), HCM; 2 seeds k=0, static, one pair: 3,836. Evaluation total 32,880 episodes; with collection 48,871.
- Outcomes per cell. Net success vs k=0; gain net of the static-procedure prompt (Measurement C); retained-gain ratio gain_R(S)/gain_R(self_R(B)) and, for backbone writers, gain_R(S)/gain_w(S), with CIs; per-type gains; retrieval-time conflict rate (fraction of top-3 sets containing >= 2 distinct skeletons for the type); below-self share (fraction of retrieved items from writers with s_w(t) < s_R(t)); injected tokens.
- Analysis. Primary: the paired contrasts of P1-P5. Secondary (P6): Spearman rho of gain-over-own-pool with frozen C across the 21 store x reader cells that contain a foreign writer, partial correlations of N, diversity class and conflict rate with C controlled, cluster-bootstrap CIs; per-type decomposition of the COV and HCM gains.
- Schedule. GPU0 serves the reader under evaluation while GPU1 collects the next writer's pool or serves the second reader. At the rate assumed for the on-disk pool (about 20 episodes/min per A100 for 32B models, about 10/min for gpt-oss-120b; re-measured in the first hour): collection 10,661 32B episodes (9 GPU-h) + 5,330 gpt-oss episodes (9 GPU-h); evaluation 29,044 32B episodes (24 GPU-h) + 3,836 gpt-oss episodes (6.4 GPU-h); about 49 GPU-h, 25 h with both A100s busy, at most 4 days with model swaps, the seed rule (<= 4,400 episodes) and a 2x throughput margin. If measured throughput is below 10 episodes/min, the 2-seed cells of the EXAONE and gpt-oss readers are cut first, then HCE; the 8-seed headline cells, HARM and self(B/2) are never cut.
Baselines and Ablations:
- k=0 memory-free reader (every reader).
- Static-procedure prompt (Measurement C), per type, every reader; every transfer gain is reported net of it.
- self_R(B) at k=3 for every reader (matched-cost self-pool control) and self(B/2) alone (what displacing half the budget costs before any writer is added; the saturation gate for P3).
- Same-headcount, same-item-count coverage contrast: COV vs DOM (only C differs).
- Equal-coverage constructions EC8, EC4-prox, EC4-cap (headcount and diversity class varied at fixed C, fixed budget and fixed per-type item counts).
- EC8-skel1 vs EC8-skelV (conflict manipulated at fixed N and C).
- Expert-only bank (Measurement A reference) with item-matched (HCM-item) and episode-matched (HCM) model-writer stores reported side by side; HCE as a secondary cell that enters no ratio.
- HARM positive control (Gate 0): manufactured wrong-procedure items planted in COV's gpt-oss half at 25% (then 50%); must cost >= 6 net vs COV or the equivalence bands of P2, P3 and P5 are declared uninterpretable. No read-time detector is proposed, so none is scored.
- Reader-as-writer cells (each backbone reads HCM and its own pairs) for the gain_R(S)/gain_w(S) ratio denominators.
- Two retrievers (BM25 on task string; dense on full item text) for the conflict-rate and below-self-share statistics, computed offline.
- Skeleton parser validated on 100 hand-labelled items before conflict rates or skeleton filtering are used.
- No trained or adapted component.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (coverage governs; closer_beats_stronger predicts the opposite). Arms: COV = self(B/2)+gpt-oss(B/2) vs DOM = self(B/2)+dominated(B/2) (same headcount, same per-type item count, same self share; only C differs) and vs SELF = self(B); Qwen3-32B reader, k=3, 274 games x 8 seeds, paired CI +/-3.2. Predicted: COV - DOM >= 6 net and COV - SELF >= 6 net, and COV beats the static-procedure prompt by >= 6 net on heat/clean/cool (about 140 games; paired about +/-6 on the subset). Falsified if the 95% CI upper bound of COV - DOM or of COV - SELF is below 6 (point estimate <= +2.8 at this noise), or if COV - static on heat/clean/cool has upper bound below 6. Secondary: HCM (N=3, B/3 each) vs SELF, 4 seeds, same rule at +/-4.5 (point <= +1.5 falsifies).
- P2 (headline: headcount and diversity class add nothing at fixed coverage). Arm (a): EC8 (equal-coverage N=8) vs COV (N=2), identical C by construction, identical per-type item counts, budget B, Qwen3-32B reader, 8 seeds each, paired +/-3.2. Predicted: |EC8 - COV| < 6 net, affirmed when the 90% CI lies inside [-6, +6] (|point| <= 3.3 at this noise). Falsified if EC8 - COV >= +6 (diversity per se helps; the Memory Sharing reading) or <= -6 (dilution or conflict costs; the contributor_conflict_not_size reading) with the 95% CI excluding 0 (an observed +/-6 has CI [2.8, 9.2]). Arm (b): EC4-cap vs EC4-prox (identical C, N and per-type counts; extra writers are other backbones vs Qwen3 variants; closer_beats_stronger predicts EC4-prox > EC4-cap), 4 seeds plus the seed rule; same band and falsifier (at 4 seeds an observed +/-6 has CI [1.5, 10.5]). Inconclusive outcomes (90% CI not inside the band and 95% CI including 0) receive 4 more seeds, cap 12.
- P3 (a dominated writer costs nothing). Arm: DOM vs SELF, 8 seeds, paired +/-3.2, TOST band +/-6. Falsified if DOM - SELF <= -6 (item count or proximity governs) or >= +6 (phrasing diversity governs) with the 95% CI excluding 0. Interpretability gate: self(B/2) alone (4 seeds) must be below SELF by >= 3 net with CI excluding 0 (the store is not saturated); if it is saturated, the displacement is rerun as self(B/4)+dominated(3B/4) vs SELF under the same rule.
- P4 (model writers recover most of the expert's contribution). Arms: HCM-item = {Qwen3 ReAct, EXAONE, gpt-oss} item-matched per type to the expert bank, expert-only bank, SELF; Qwen3-32B reader, 4 seeds plus the seed rule, heat/clean/cool. Predicted: (gain_HCM-item - gain_SELF) / (gain_expert - gain_SELF) >= 0.6 on those types. Falsified if the ratio is <= 0.4 with the joint-bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0.6. HCE is reported alongside but enters no ratio.
- P5 (conflict does not govern at fixed coverage; manipulated). Arms: EC8-skelV vs EC8-skel1 (same eight writers, identical C and per-type counts; retrieval conflict rate manipulated), Qwen3-32B reader, 4 seeds plus the seed rule. Manipulation check: conflict rate in EC8-skelV >= EC8-skel1 + 0.30 absolute under both retrievers; if not met, P5 is reported as not tested. Predicted: |skelV - skel1| < 6 net (TOST band +/-6). Falsified if skelV - skel1 <= -6 with the 95% CI excluding 0 (conflict governs; contributor_conflict_not_size is rescued) or >= +6 (skeleton diversity helps). Conflict rate vs N over {1, 2, 3, 4, 8} is logged as a description and carries no claim.
- P6 (secondary: C is a pre-read predictor). Across the 21 store x reader cells that contain a foreign writer, Spearman rho between gain over the reader's own matched pool and the frozen C is >= 0.6, with a cluster-bootstrap 95% CI (games resampled jointly across cells, 10,000 resamples) excluding 0. Falsified if the CI includes 0 or the point estimate is below 0.3. Partial correlations of N, diversity class and conflict rate with C controlled are reported with the same CIs as descriptions; the decisive tests of N, class and conflict are P2 and P5. Cell noise (+/-8 at 2 seeds) attenuates rho toward 0 and is stated with the result.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired design on the same 274 validation games (seen+unseen) x seeds; per-game differences bootstrapped over games (10,000 resamples) with seeds as blocks. Cell CIs: +/-8 net at 2 seeds, +/-5.7 at 4, +/-4.0 at 8; paired differences +/-6.4, +/-4.5, +/-3.2. Margins are fractions of the Gate-0 effect of 6 net. Directional claims (P1) use the full effect and are falsified when the 95% CI upper bound falls below 6. Equivalence claims (P2, P3, P5) use two one-sided tests at alpha = 0.05 with band +/-6 (the 90% CI must lie inside [-6, +6]): at 8 seeds this affirms equivalence when |d| <= 3.3, with power 0.96 at d = 0 and 0.79 at |d| = 2, and is falsified when |d| >= 6 with the 95% CI excluding 0 (an observed +/-6 has CI [2.8, 9.2]); at 4 seeds affirmation needs |d| <= 2.2 (power 0.66 at d = 0), so the pre-registered seed rule adds 4 seeds (cap 12; at most 4 cells, <= 4,400 episodes) to any contrast that is neither affirmed nor falsified. Sub-Gate-0 effects with CIs excluding 0 are reported as real but within the band, not as falsifications. Positive control: HARM must cost >= 6 net vs COV (Gate 0) at 25% or 50% planting; otherwise the equivalence claims are declared uninterpretable. Per-type claims use the type's game count (heat/clean/cool about 140 games; paired about +/-6 at 4 seeds, +/-4.5 at 8 on the subset) and carry their own CIs; ratio CIs by joint bootstrap over games across numerator and denominator arms. C, the equal-coverage restrictions and the skeleton filters are computed from collection logs and the parser, and frozen before the first evaluation cell. Reader decoding fixed (T=0 or fixed sampling seed); environment seeds fixed; same retriever and injection for every cell; injected tokens per episode reported for every cell; all transfer gains reported net of the static-procedure prompt; retained-gain ratios per writer x reader cell with CIs. Correlational statistics (P6) use a cluster bootstrap resampling games jointly across cells and are reported with the attenuation implied by +/-8 cell noise.

Risk Factors and Limitations: gpt-oss-120b and EXAONE-4.0-32B serving unverified (fallback: proximity axis only, capability axis carried by expert vs self, P4 dropped). If all writers share the same weak types, C is small everywhere: COV - DOM is then a null with a measured C, the equivalence claims are trivially met, and the study reports the coverage range actually spanned. The equal-coverage restriction drops items on coverage-raising types, so EC8, EC4-prox and EC4-cap have provenance spread across writers but the same per-type counts as COV; the equalization is symmetric and can reduce COV's counts. T=1.2 may not be dominated on every type (handled by construction at the cost of a smaller dominated share). Skeleton filtering may fail to move the conflict rate by 0.30, in which case P5 is reported untested. The expert writer breaks episode-cost matching (item-matched accounting only). ALFWorld's six types give a coarse coverage statistic. Equivalence bands are the full Gate-0 effect; headcount, class or conflict effects smaller than 6 net are not claimed absent. Throughput is assumed, not measured, for gpt-oss-120b (no native MXFP4 on A100); the pre-registered cut order protects the headline cells. P6 is attenuated by +/-8 noise on 2-seed cells and is secondary to the manipulations.
Addresses gap: G12 (value and contamination of a shared store vs number and diversity of writers, as manipulated contrasts at matched cost); secondarily G14 (self-collected control at matched cost).
Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: 'Two writers for one task set exist on disk ... type-skewed' records the writers' profiles; this idea claims the profiles' complement predicts what a population store adds and that headcount, diversity class and conflict do not, and tests each by construction: an equal-coverage N=8 vs N=2 store, equal-coverage proximity vs capability N=4 stores, skeleton-matched vs skeleton-varied stores, and a dominated-writer displacement, none of which the bullet can supply. Nearest digest card: 2404.09982 claims that diversity of shared in-context memories improves performance; this idea claims that at matched budget and fixed coverage diversity adds less than the Gate-0 effect and tests it with a powered two-one-sided-test design. Nearest archived ideas: contributor_conflict_not_size, where conflict was a property of the construction, here conflict is manipulated at fixed coverage and predicted not to govern; closer_beats_stronger, where proximity predicted transfer, here a far-but-covering writer is predicted to help and a near-but-dominated writer to add nothing.
Changes made:
- P2 (headline; was unresolvable): replaced the correlation-over-12-cells test with a powered paired manipulation, EC8 (equal-coverage N=8) vs COV (N=2) at identical C and per-type item counts, 8 seeds each (paired +/-3.2), two one-sided tests with band +/-6 = the Gate-0 effect, falsified at |diff| >= 6 with the 95% CI excluding 0; the class clause is now its own paired contrast (EC4-cap vs EC4-prox at identical C). The correlation survives as secondary P6 with a cluster-bootstrap CI over 21 cells and a reachable falsifier (CI includes 0).
- P3 (was unresolvable): seeds raised to 8, equivalence band widened from +/-4 to the Gate-0 +/-6 with falsification at +/-6 outside a CI excluding 0, TOST rule pre-registered with stated power (0.96 at d = 0), and a saturation gate (self(B/2) alone) with a 3B/4 displacement fallback.
- P4 (was near-entailed): numerator is now the model-writers-only store {Qwen3 ReAct, EXAONE, gpt-oss} item-matched per type to the expert bank; the expert-containing HCE is a secondary cell that enters no ratio.
- P5 (was unresolvable): conflict is manipulated rather than observed, skeleton-matched vs skeleton-varied N=8 stores at identical C, N and item counts, with a manipulation check (>= 0.30 conflict-rate gap) and a paired falsifier; the conflict-rises-with-N clause is demoted to a logged description.
- P1 (was open but expert-loaded): the expert quarter is removed from the capability-diverse store; the powered primary contrast is COV vs DOM (same headcount, same item count, only C differs) and COV vs SELF at 8 seeds; the headroom-forced localization clause is dropped.
- Added the HARM positive control (Gate 0, planted wrong items by writer identity at controlled rates) so the equivalence results are interpretable, per the brief's contamination rule; no detector is proposed, so none is scored.
- Grid: k=1 cells cut (they carried no claim); gpt-oss plan-then-act added as the eighth writer for N=8; cell-by-cell episode counts and GPU-hours stated (32,880 evaluation + 15,991 collection episodes, about 49 GPU-h, at most 4 days on both A100s) with a pre-registered cut order.
- Sharpness kept: the central nulls (headcount, class and conflict add less than the Gate-0 effect at fixed coverage; a dominated writer costs nothing) are now tested as manipulations with pre-registered equivalence bands that the rivals (Memory Sharing's diversity-helps, contributor_conflict_not_size's conflict-hurts, closer_beats_stronger's proximity-governs) predict to fail; the coverage claim remains a >= 6 net directional prediction and C remains a frozen pre-read predictor.
